designVerdict: REJECTED - not fitted. The enable path needs no transistor and the FAULT interlock uses BSS138.
notes: THE FAULT INTERLOCK NEEDS TWO DEVICES, NOT ONE. A MOSFET drain is a single node, so one device tied to both UVLO pins would short the two dividers together and each enable transistor would then disable both channels, destroying independent per-channel shedding.
SUPERSEDED: earlier notes here described level-shifting a 36 V P-FET gate off the HUSB238A GATE pin, and gave a count of three. Neither is the circuit; that topology does not exist in the design.

ROLE CHANGED with the move from LM5069 to TPS16630. They now pull SHDN low rather than a UVLO divider node. SHDN is active-low shutdown, so a 100 kOhm PULL-DOWN on the pin is the fail-safe direction and firmware drives the GPIO HIGH to enable - the inverted logic the LM5069 arrangement needed is gone. The FAULT interlock still needs one device per channel, since one drain tied to both SHDN pins would couple the channels.

SCOPE REDUCED: the FAULT interlock moved to BSS138 (C7420339), whose 1.6 V max threshold suits the HUSB238A's 2.64 V V_OH. These two keep the enable role, where a full 3.3 V gate drive makes the threshold irrelevant.

RETIRED. Earlier revisions used it for a high-side P-FET gate shift, then for an LM5069 UVLO pull-down, then for the TPS16630 SHDN enable. None of those exist: SHDN is a logic input the GPIO drives directly through a 1 kOhm series resistor, and the FAULT interlock moved to BSS138 because its 1.5 V max threshold suits the HUSB238A's 2.64 V V_OH where this part's 2.5 V max does not.
